== Overview ==

Game server responsibilities (authentication, matchmaking, UGC, etc.) are organized into separate protocols, sometimes also seen called "services", with each protocol having a series of methods representing specific actions a server/client can make. A game server may have any number of protocols implemented (so long as there are not protocol ID conflicts), and can selectively enable/disable entire protocols/specific protocol methods at will to fit the games needs. That being said, there are 2 requirements:

# The games authentication server MUST implement [[Online/Nintendo_Network/NEX/Protocols/TicketGrantingProtocol|TicketGrantingProtocol]]. This is required for the client to validate itself and obtain the location of the games secure server. It may implement others, though NEX never does.
# The games secure server MUST implement [[Online/Nintendo_Network/NEX/Protocols/SecureConnectionProtocol|SecureConnectionProtocol]]. This is required to fully register the clients connection with the game server, to gain access to the other protocols.

The flexible nature of Rendez-Vous also allows a developer to customize/modify existing protocols, or create entirely custom ones, to meet a games requirements. These changes will also be documented on their own pages. There are also a number of "internal" protocols, which are assumed to be used internally by the game servers for various tasks, though some game clients have references to them.

Each protocol is assigned a unique protocol ID, with multiple ranges of protocol IDs for different use cases. Information about these protocols can be obtained by scanning games [[Online/Nintendo_Network/NEX/DDL|DDL information]] and reverse engineering game clients, since every game client also contains code to handle requests that normally only servers would recieve (game servers are effectively more-or-less just another Rendez-Vous client being connected to).

{| class="wikitable"
|-
! Range !! Name !! Description
|-
| 1-99 || Core || Protocols designed and provided by Quazal. These protocols perform critical operations all game servers could need. Developers can extend the functionality of these protocols by adding/modifying protocol methods, but the protocols themselves are never outright replaced by a given game for any custom purposes.
|-
| 100+ || Developer || Protocols unique to a specific game. A developer creating multiple games may share these protocols between games, such as Nintendo with NEX, but that is not guaranteed. As a rule of thumb, all protocols with IDs 100+ should be assumed to be game-specific.
|-
| 200+ || Nintendo reserved || Nintendo appears to have added their own range of "reserved" protocol IDs on top of the developer range. This range seems to allow developers to add game-specific protocols on top of the common protocols provided by NEX. Similar conventions may exist in other titles, but this is not guaranteed. As a rule of thumb, all protocols with IDs 100+ should be assumed to be game-specific.
|}

== Internal protocols ==

These protocols seem to be used internally by the servers. Likely for their inter-server communications. Many of these can only be observed through the [[Online/Nintendo_Network/NEX/Protocols/Debug|Debug]] protocol. However some games implement subsets of these protocols.
